Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency & errors hitting our inference; urgent

Short updates from infra traces:
- Envoy at edge pod eu-west-1b servicing Stratford shows sustained downstream queue depths increasing ~3x from baseline starting 13:48 PST. Logs show repeated upstream 504/502 when Envoy's connection pool hits per-worker fd limits.
- NAT conntrack counters on the customer's peering VLAN show spikes concurrent with the issue (we're ingesting their v4 flows). Possibility: their NAT gateway is running low on ephemeral ports causing TCP reuse delays.
- No BGP flap logged on our peering fabric in the last 24h, but I see route preference differences — some flows are being steered through our fallback region causing cross-region hairpins (latency added).

Attaching envoy queue snippet and pcaps (summary). Recommend: 1) temporarily shift Stratford traffic to our reserved fallback pool in us-west-2 to relieve hairpinning; 2) ask Stratford to confirm NAT ephemeral exhaustion and check their route tables; 3) increase per-worker fd soft limit on affected edge nodes.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Eng
[Attachment: envoy_queues_20281203.log] [Attachment: pcap_summary.txt]

Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 15:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & errors hitting our inference; urgent

Tom — thanks for the traces. Quick summary of what we've found and immediate mitigation plan:

Executive summary (short):
- Root signals point to a combination of (A) asymmetric routing causing cross-region hairpin to a fallback pool and (B) downstream proxy/Envoy queueing with FD limits hitting under Stratford's flow pattern. There is a strong signal that Stratford's NAT gateway may be exhausting ephemeral ports which amplifies connection churn.

Immediate actions (we've already initiated):
1) Traffic shift: routing Stratford to our reserved us-west-2 pool (expected latency change: -300–400ms p95) — in-flight now.
2) Edge tuning: raised per-worker fd soft limits and increased Envoy connection pool size on affected nodes.
3) Monitoring: enabled more aggressive tracing and pcap capture for 2h window and created JIRA-RT-4821 for follow-up.

What we need from you:
- Can your network team confirm VPC route tables and NAT ephemeral port utilization? If NAT ports are saturated, please increase ephemeral port range or add SNAT pool.
- Share any recent firewall/proxy changes on your side (ACLs, IP binding).

I'll keep you updated; aiming for full recovery in the next 45–90 minutes. If we don't see recovery in that window, I'll escalate to exec ready brief.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & errors hitting our inference; urgent

Post-mitigation check:
- Traffic shift completed at 15:45 PST; metrics show p95 reduced from ~850ms to ~270ms and 5xx down to 0.6% within 18 minutes. Throughput recovered to ~94% of baseline.
- Envoy queue depth returned to normal after fd increase; no persistent crashes.
- DNS checks: discovered a split-horizon config on Stratford's side where internal records for api.stratford-retail.com returned a different /24 in one AZ — that can cause asymmetric peering selection. Jonas is coordinating a short doc for their network team.

Next steps for postmortem:
- Joint RCA with Stratford networking ops: confirm NAT ephemeral health, align route preferences so we avoid hairpin pathing, and standardize split-horizon records.
- Recommend we offer a short-runbook for Stratford to handle ephemeral exhaustion and a pre-approved traffic-shift playbook for future incidents.

— Vivek
Head of Platform Reliability
